one_month_reasoning: No AAOI-specific scheduled event falls inside 2026-10-02 to 2026-11-01. Q3 2026 results are estimated for about Nov 5. Prior Q3 prints came on 2025-11-06 and 2024-11-07, and no date 8-K has been filed (supervisor, src 36), so I put only ~5-10% on an in-window print or pre-announcement. In the window: hyperscaler Q3 capex calls (~Oct 27-30) that move the whole AI-optics group, and ongoing sales under the $600M ATM (src 4, 35), a mild supply overhang. The run-up into the Q4-guide test (~$485M needed for the ~$1.1B FY26 target vs ~$425M consensus-implied) cuts both ways. I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred slightly below spot (median ~$114) with monthly sigma 0.37 (139%/3.5 ≈ 0.40, shaded for no scheduled company event). That gives P(>= spot) 0.485.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (60%): NTM-at-Oct-2027 EPS $4.80 x 19x = $91, and EV/EBITDA (40%): NTM EBITDA $600M x 14x + $0.25B net cash over ~98M diluted shares = $88. Blended ~$90. Both multiples sit inside a 10-peer CY2027 range (P/E median 21.6x).

inputs_detail.input: Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA and non-GAAP tax add-back
inputs_detail.derivation: The $0.06 non-GAAP EPS rests on the tax line, so operating leverage has not yet appeared.

Revenue ~$2.4B (below the $2.66B consensus) x 31% non-GAAP GM = $744M, less ~$320M non-GAAP opex (GAAP opex was $77.9M/qtr in Q2 and rising), 15% tax, ~97M shares. About 17% below the $4.60 consensus, which needs ~33% GM against 29.8% in Q2.
Revenue ~$3.2B as capacity reaches 930k units/month by end-2027, 32% GM, ~$380M opex, 15% tax, ~99M shares.
0.25 x $3.80 + 0.75 x $5.50 = $5.08, less a ~5% execution haircut because no pre-tax operating profit has been shown yet.

10-peer CY2027 P/E median 21.6x (range 10.9x-47.8x, all converted to calendar 2027). I apply 19x to a year-forward NTM EPS at the horizon: ~12% below today's median for expected multiple compression as peer growth decelerates over the year, plus a discount for concentration and funding risk. That is inside the range and between FN (23.2x) and JBL/SANM (15.9x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM revenue $3.0B x 20% = $600M EBITDA x 14x = $8.4B EV + $0.25B net cash; /98M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x CY27 $2.4B + 0.75 x CY28 $3.2B; consistent with 650k units/month by YE2026 and 930k by end-2027.
GM ~32% less ~12.5% non-GAAP opex plus ~4% D&A ≈ 23%, cut to 20% because Adjusted EBITDA was -$0.5M in Q2 2026.

Peer CY2027 EV/EBITDA proxy median 16.7x (range 10.3x-45.2x; trailing EV/EBITDA scaled by CY27/TTM revenue at constant margin). 14x is inside the range, discounted for the same compression and risk reasons as the P/E.
At 2026-06-30: cash and restricted cash $508.8M, converts $129.1M, other debt ~$57M, bank acceptances $33.9M, so ~$0.29-0.32B. H2 capex above H1's $625M absorbs the ATM proceeds.
84.9M outstanding Aug 20 + ~5.2M ATM shares at ~$115 + 2.9M convert shares + ~1.0M vested Amazon warrant (treasury method) + 1.7M RSU/PSU ≈ 95.7M, plus a buffer for a further raise.

bear.story: A 2017/2025 replay. The Q4 guide misses the ~$485M implied step, or a top-3 customer (92% of revenue) digests or dual-sources. GM stays below 30%, capex is not recovered, and more dilution follows. 2027 EPS ~$1.5-2 at a low peer multiple. After its prior +100% years AAOI fell 27-62% in the next year (2017-18), with an average -44% peak-to-trough in shocks.

base.story: The ramp is delivered with slippage: CY27 revenue ~$2.2-2.6B, GM ~31%, EPS ~$3.5-4.2. The multiple compresses toward a ~19-20x NTM inside the direct-peer range as growth normalises, and dilution reaches ~98M shares. The stock ends a little below spot.

bull.story: Q4 2026 confirms ~$485M and GM above 31%. Demand outruns capacity through 2027, 930k units/month is reached, and the 1.6T mix lifts the Q4-27 run rate above $3.5B and EPS run rate to $8+. A ~25x multiple holds and the stock revisits the May-2026 high area.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 10.9x (Eoptolink) to 47.8x (Accelink); CY2027 EV/EBITDA proxy 10.3x (Jabil) to 45.2x (Lumentum). One basis throughout: every P/E is price / calendar-2027 consensus EPS. June-FY names (COHR, LITE, FN) use the average of FY27 and FY28, JBL uses 8/12 FY27 + 4/12 FY28 (Aug FY), and SANM uses 9/12 FY27 + 3/12 of an extrapolated FY28 (its data is stale, Jul 28). StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' was not used because it mixes bases: Innolight's 15.75x is neither CY26 (27.0x) nor CY27 (12.2x).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19x NTM-at-horizon P/E and 14x EV/EBITDA, both inside the peer range and ~12-16% below the medians (21.5x / 16.7x). Today AAOI trades at 25.1x CY27 consensus ($115.59 / $4.60), a ~16% premium to the median, and at ~30x my own CY27 EPS of $3.80.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is used. The modest discount has two parts. (1) Timing: I apply the multiple to a year-forward NTM EPS at Oct-2027, when peers' growth (CY27 EPS +15% to +122%) will have decelerated, so today's CY27 median overstates the horizon multiple. (2) Structural features that persist through the horizon, from filings: 92% top-3 customer concentration (10-Q), negative operating cash flow with capex funded by three 2026 equity raises and a live $600M ATM, and Adjusted EBITDA of -$0.5M in Q2 2026. The low-GM Chinese module makers (Accelink, Huagong) trade at 35-48x, but on much smaller growth-adjusted EPS bases and in a different market, so they do not justify a premium for AAOI. AAOI's possible US/Texas-capacity advantage if China-made modules are restricted is unproven in pricing, so it is not used.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$62 (under the July-2026 low of $76, ~13x my $4.80 NTM EPS, ~13.5x the $4.60 CY27 consensus) the market would be pricing CY27 EPS near $2-2.5. That would mean a missed Q4 2026 step, a cut at one of the three customers that make up 92% of revenue, or GM stuck below 30% with $1B+ of capex unrecovered, rather than ordinary 139%-vol noise.

reasoning: Base rates still anchor the shape. From AAOI's own 2016-2026 monthly history (src 9) the unconditional 12-month forward return is extremely wide (10th/50th/90th pct about -63%/-5%/+454%, up in only 49% of months). After +100% years the next 12 months ranged from -27% to -62% (2017) to large further gains (2023-24, 2025). Trefis (src 10) counts 10 shocks averaging -44%, and the 2017 single-customer collapse and the 2000-02 optical bust (src 11-14) show how fast component demand can halve. Round 2 corrections from the supervisor's fact-check, which I verified in the Q2 8-K (src 1): (a) the $0.06 non-GAAP EPS rests on a $14.262M tax add-back and Adjusted EBITDA was -$0.543M, so margin expansion is still a forecast, and I cut my EBITDA margin to 20% and CY27 EPS to $3.80; (b) net cash is ~$0.25B, not $0.6B (cash $508.8M, converts $129.1M, other debt, H2 capex); (c) ~98M diluted shares, not 102M; (d) my peer median was on a mixed basis. I rebuilt the comps on one calendar-2027 basis from StockAnalysis annual consensus (src 24-33): 10 optical-module and optics-manufacturing peers, P/E median 21.6x (10.9x-47.8x), EV/EBITDA proxy median 16.7x. Fabless semis and systems names are dropped, Accelink and Huagong are added as low-GM module makers, and JBL and SANM are added as manufacturing peers. One disagreement with the supervisor: StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' for Innolight/Eoptolink is not CY27 (CY27 is 12.2x/10.9x), so the direct-peer CY27 median is a little lower than it states once that is fixed, but my broader set lands at ~21.6x. Fair value falls from $106 to ~$90 (P/E $91, EV/EBITDA $88), below spot. The distribution is a lognormal mixture: bear $40 (26%, sigma 0.5), base $103 (45%, sigma 0.33), bull $210 (29%, sigma 0.36). The bull weight stays near 30% because >$200M of 1.6T orders and demand above capacity through mid-2027 are real (src 2), and the stock has already halved from its May high. That gives a median ~$105, P(>=116) 0.44 (from 0.48), P(<58) ~22% and P(>=231) ~12%. Prediction-market inputs (src 15-21) are macro context only, as the supervisor noted, and do not move numbers. Research limits: forward EBITDA is not available on the free source, so EV/EBITDA comps are proxies, and CIG (603083) and Linktel (301205) were excluded because no consensus forecast was available.
